label: GaAs p-n junction laser diode, about 0.4 mm cube, two polished parallel faces, pulsed in liquid nitrogen (diodes L-69, L-70)
core_material: GaAs p-n junction between degenerate n- and p-type regions; junction in a horizontal plane through the cube centre
notes: Diodes described approximately as cubes 0.4 mm on an edge, front and back faces polished parallel to each other and perpendicular to the junction; Ohmic contacts on top and bottom; 5-20 us current pulses, diode immersed in liquid nitrogen (p.1). Diodes L-69 (Fig. 1-2) and L-70 (p.2, Fig. 3) are entered as one design (c1), the diode named in each metric condition; diode L-75 of 'quite different characteristics' (p.3) has no number. Temperature not printed (liquid nitrogen only), so temperature_k is empty. No fabrication statement: fab empty. Not entered: threshold near 8500 A/cm2 for L-70, linear below 5000 A/cm2, about ten times the extrapolated intensity at 20000 A/cm2 (p.2; no threshold-current-density parameter, registry gap); spectral width at half maximum 125 Angstrom below and 15 Angstrom above threshold (p.2; the paper does not call it a 3-dB width and laser has no FWHM parameter, registry gap); instrument resolution about 3 Angstrom (p.2); extra-mode separation stated only as about three times the calculated value (p.2, no number); L-75 vertical pattern 'a few tenths of a degree' and coherence over about 100 um (p.3, no single value).

label: Ga(As1-xPx) p-n junction laser diode 28A, polished parallel faces, visible (about 7100 Angstrom), 77 K pulsed
core_material: diffused p-n junction in n-type Ga(As1-xPx) (halogen vapor transport and synthesis; donor concentration above 1e18 cm-3), junction 10 um or deeper below one contact surface
notes: Diodes are rectangular parallelepipeds or cubes with two opposite parallel sides polished, active (junction) area about 1e-3 cm2, junction perpendicular to the polished faces (p.2); composition x not stated. Fab: 'Most of our diodes have been fabricated on n-type Ga(As1-xPx), prepared by the ... procedure we have previously described' (p.2) is passive for the diodes and first-person only for the material; acknowledgment thanks four named people for substantial contributions to the fabrication of the junctions (p.3) with no org named; both authors at General Electric Company, Syracuse (not in the registry). Fab left empty (coordinator to rule; General Electric missing from organizations.csv). Not entered: threshold about 11,000 A/cm2 (p.2, no threshold-current-density parameter, registry gap); spectral widths about 125 Angstrom near threshold, about 20 Angstrom at 16,000 A/cm2 and about 12 Angstrom at 19,000 A/cm2 (p.2, Fig. 1; no laser FWHM parameter, registry gap); wavelength 'can be selected' from perhaps below 6200 to near 8400 Angstrom (p.3, a statement on the alloy system, not a measured tuning range); 20 to over 100 mA in free air at 300 K giving perceptible red emission (p.2, no output value).

label: GaAs Zn-diffused p-n junction diode (1e-4 cm2 etched junction) showing stimulated-emission line narrowing, no resonant cavity, 77 K
core_material: Zn diffused into Te-doped GaAs; etched junction mesa bonded on a Au-plated kovar washer with an In dot contact (Fig. 1 inset)
notes: 'No attempt was made to obtain highly resonant electromagnetic modes' (p.2): entered as laser.other because papers.csv lists the paper as a laser demonstration and the authors report stimulated emission; the device has no stated optical cavity. Diodes immersed in liquid nitrogen (abstract: 77 K), current pulses as short as 50 ns at high current (p.2). Fab: passive 'were made by diffusing Zn into GaAs' (p.2): fab empty. Not entered: linewidth narrowing by more than 20 times to less than kT/5 (p.2) and the Fig. 1 widths (no laser FWHM parameter, registry gap; widths above 10 A are stated as upper limits because of junction heating, p.3); quantum efficiency per injected electron greater than 0.2, perhaps close to 1, above 10 A/cm2 (p.3, no external-quantum-efficiency parameter for lasers, registry gap); two lines about 6 Angstrom apart and 2 Angstrom wide 'in one diode' at the highest currents (p.3; sample not identified with the Fig. 1 diode, D159); the 100 photons per mode figure (p.3, calculation).

label: GaAs diffused-junction line-mesa laser diode, 1.4 x 0.6 mm junction, polished short sides, pulsed at 77 K and 4.2 K
core_material: GaAs diffused p-n junction, line mesa structure; short sides polished optically flat and nearly parallel
notes: Junction area 1.4 x 0.6 mm with the short sides polished (p.2); the cavity length is not stated explicitly, so no length row. Strauss of Lincoln Laboratory (p.3; material supplier note). Fab: acknowledgment thanks W. H. Laswell for polishing the junctions and F. M. Sullivan and P. A. Gagnon for fabricating the diodes (p.3), with no org named for them; all authors at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. Fab left empty (staff thanks without a named org; coordinator to rule, org_mit_lincoln_laboratory is the candidate).
